subject: POC trial: model selection & evaluation plan
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@acmehealth.com>, David Lee <david.lee@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 05 May 2026 14:10:00 -0700
Subject: POC trial: model selection & evaluation plan

Thanks again for taking the call this morning — really appreciate the time. Below is a concise recap and a proposed evaluation plan for the POC so we can lock scope and timeline. Please flag anything missing or incorrect.

High-level goal:
- Validate model choice and integration approach for Acme Health's clinical triage assistant (multi-turn triage, entity extraction, and instruction-following).

Primary success criteria (customer-facing):
- Accuracy / quality: intent/entity extraction F1 >= 0.85 on the annotated validation set; end-to-end task satisfaction >= 90% on labeled prompts.
- Latency: inference p95 <= 200ms for single-turn queries (target for hosted endpoint with batch-friendly traffic).
- Cost: per-token/inference unit cost within target (goal: <$0.05 per 1k tokens for generation workload; we can tighten after initial bench).
- Security/privacy: data stays within approved controls (HIPAA-aware handling; Redwood private deployment or VPC if required).

Evaluation plan & milestones (4-week baseline POC):
- Week 0 (Kickoff): confirm SOW, exchange sample datasets (anonymized), get any compliance checklist in-flight, and agree on measurement scripts.
- Week 1 (Setup): provisioning + baseline benchmark on 2 model variants; integration of API + auth.
- Week 2 (Model tuning & bench): run quality evaluation (gold prompts, NLU metrics) and latency/cost profiling; produce initial results.
- Week 3 (Integration + safety): integration tests, filtering/safety checks, multilingual tests (see note below).
- Week 4 (Decision & next steps): review results, align on production plan (Dedicated/Private), and agree on final model and rollout path.

Model selection (proposed for trial):
- Primary candidate: Llama 2 13B (quantized FP16/INT8 where possible) — good quality/latency balance for instruction following and multi-turn.
- High-accuracy option (if you want top quality testing): Llama 2 70B (higher cost, higher accuracy) — run as a controlled test if accuracy delta matters.
- Fallback / low-cost variant: Mistral-7B (quantized) for budget-constrained paths and as an automated fallback for spikes.
- Multilingual: we recommend evaluating Spanish first (primary for your users), then French and Portuguese. For Spanish-heavy intents we may apply LoRA or small fine-tune on anonymized examples.

Ownership:
- Redwood: Ben Carter (sales lead) and Marissa Cole (solutions engineer) — responsible for provisioning, bench scripts, and model tuning.
- Acme: Alice Johnson (product lead) and David Lee (engineering) — provide sample data, security contacts, and decision authority.

Deliverables & artifacts:
- ACME_POC_SOW.pdf (attached) — scope & acceptance criteria.
- Benchmark report (week 2): latency, cost, quality metrics per model.
- Eval harness & prompts (shared Drive link).

Next steps (ask):
1) Please confirm that the success criteria above match your expectations.
2) Share anonymized sample dataset and any security questionnaire items we should prioritize (SOC2/HIPAA controls).
3) Confirm kickoff availability: propose Thu May 7 10:00-11:00 AM PT or Fri May 8 1:00-2:00 PM PT.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this moving.

--
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
(415) 555-0192
From: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@acmehealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: David Lee <david.lee@acmehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 06 May 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC trial: model selection & evaluation plan

Hi Ben — thanks for the detailed recap. This looks good and covers most of what we talked about. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Multilingual: Spanish is our highest priority (roughly 30% of user traffic), so we need to ensure the primary model handles Spanish well out-of-the-box or via light tuning. French/Portuguese are lower priority.
- Compliance: we will need to route POC traffic through our VPC endpoint and require a short SOC2/HIPAA attestation before starting. I'll attach the security questionnaire we started — can your security/solutions team confirm the items? (attached: ACME_security_questions.xlsx)
- Timeline: procurement here tends to add a week or two; realistically we may be closer to a 6-week timeline unless we can overlap procurement with engineering work. Okay to start with sandbox data while procurement completes?

Can Marissa (cc'ed) confirm whether the Llama 2 13B path supports Spanish without significant fine-tuning, and what the incremental cost/time would be for a LoRA on ~5k examples.

Also: quick note on attachments — I uploaded a small set of anonymized prompts (clinical triage examples) to the Drive link you shared.

Thanks,
Alice
Product Lead, Acme Health
alice.johnson@acmehealth.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@acmehealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 06 May 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC trial: model selection & evaluation plan

Thanks Alice — quick technical notes from the SE side. Short answers up front: Llama 2 13B generally performs well in Spanish for instruction-following, but quality on domain-specific clinical language will improve with a small LoRA/fine-tune (~2k-5k anonymized examples). That can usually be done in ~3-5 days of compute if we prioritize it in Week 2.

Model strategy (recommended):
- Baseline: Llama 2 13B (quantized) for initial integration and latency/cost profiling.
- Golden test: Llama 2 70B run on a subset of prompts to measure peak accuracy delta (not recommended for full traffic during POC due to cost).
- Fallback: Mistral-7B quantized for lower-cost scenarios and autoscale fallback.

Evaluation specifics:
- Quality: we will run an NLU eval for intent/entity extraction (F1) and an end-to-end human-rated prompt set (Likert 1-5) for instruction-following. Please pull a 500-example validation set from your anonymized prompts for Week 2.
- Latency/cost: p95 latency tests with realistic traffic (1-5 qps) and cold/warm cache scenarios. We will provide a cost model (tokens/sec, GPU hours) in the Week 2 benchmark report.
- Safety/compliance: Redwood can run the POC inside a VPC/private deployment; we'll also provide a minimal data flow diagram and the SOC2/HIPAA points you asked about. Aditya will coordinate the security responses.

Small ops notes:
- Please give us an export of the sample prompts in CSV with a column for "expected_response" if you have labeled outputs. That speeds automated scoring.
- If you want to prioritize Spanish, we recommend a small initial LoRA and evaluate delta vs baseline (no-tune) in the Week 2 bench.

Next step from me: I'll prepare an eval harness (scripts + initial seed prompts) and share a short runbook for the LoRA workflow.

--
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@acmehealth.com>

Date: Fri, 07 May 2026 09:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC trial: model selection & evaluation plan

Great — thanks Alice/Marissa. Sounds like we have alignment: go ahead with the 13B baseline + LoRA for Spanish, run 70B as a gated accuracy test, and keep Mistral-7B as fallback. We'll treat procurement as parallel work and start sandbox integration with your anonymized prompts.

Confirming the kickoff: Thu May 7 10:00 AM PT works for Redwood. I'll send a calendar invite and attach the SOW.

Action items:
- Alice: upload 500 validation examples (CSV) and confirm security contact for the SOC2 items.
- Marissa/Aditya: share eval harness + runbook and SOC2/HIPAA attestation response.
- Ben: send calendar invite and final SOW (attached).

Thanks everyone — looking forward to the kickoff.

--
Ben
